Both findings recorded. Here's the summary:

## Results

**Report written to**: `case-studies/crossbeam-deque/spec/confirmed-bugs.md`

### Findings Summary (10 reviewed, 2 confirmed)

| # | Finding | Source | Status | Severity |
|---|---------|--------|--------|----------|
| **1** | Missing buffer re-check at LIFO first CAS in `steal_batch_with_limit_and_pop` (line 1191) | MC + Code Review | CONFIRMED (code audit) | Low — defense-in-depth gap |
| **2** | `Injector` Debug impl displays `"Worker { .. }"` (line 2169) | Code Review | CONFIRMED (code audit) | Cosmetic |
| 3-7 | CVE-2021-32810 reproduction, FIFO rollback, batch steal, single-element contention, self-steal guard | MC | FALSE POSITIVE | — |
| 8-10 | Volatile UB, epoch lifecycle, injector obstruction-freedom | Code Review | Not a bug (known) | — |

### Key Takeaway

**crossbeam-deque is correct under normal operation.** The only actionable finding is Bug 1: the CVE-2021-32810 fix (PR #726) was incompletely applied — it added buffer re-checks at 5 of 6 CAS sites but missed the LIFO first CAS in `steal_batch_and_pop` (later refactored into `steal_batch_with_limit_and_pop`). This is **not independently exploitable** because the epoch pin keeps the old buffer alive and its data is frozen/valid after resize. Model checking exhaustively verified 8.3M states with this re-check disabled — all safety invariants pass. The fix is a one-line addition for consistency.
